# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Deaf monkey, so I can see the bomb but can't hear anything, can't touch it, and hold no manual. My job is to describe what I see so Mute can match it to the manual and Blind can act.

What I observe: DISPLAY shows 3. LIGHT is purple. WIRES: 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green.

Since I speak, Mute and Blind receive my words. I'll describe everything clearly. I'll also gesture to Mute (only Mute sees gestures) — but gestures only help if we've agreed on meaning, and we haven't yet, so plain speech is safest. I'll send my full description to both.

Let me report the complete visual state so Mute can consult the manual and Blind can be told what to do.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. Bomb reads: DISPLAY shows the number 3. LIGHT is purple. Five wires: 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green. I cannot touch or read the manual. Tell me and Blind what to do.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here. Bomb reads: DISPLAY shows 3. LIGHT is purple. Five wires: 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green. Wait for Mute's instruction from the manual.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]

I'm Deaf. Mute just sent me a gesture: five fists (✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊). I can see gestures. But a gesture means nothing until we've agreed on a meaning — and we haven't established any code. Five fists could mean anything: "five wires," "wire 5," "stop," a count, etc. I shouldn't guess wildly.

However, I should note: Mute can read the manual but cannot speak. Mute's only output channel is gestures (to me, Deaf). So Mute is trying to communicate via gesture. Five ✊ symbols is likely significant — possibly "all five wires" or a count of 5, or referencing wire 5.

But I can't be sure. I can't hear, but I CAN speak — my speech reaches Mute and Blind. So I can ask Mute to clarify, or propose a code. But Mute can't speak back; Mute can only gesture. And Blind can't see gestures. So the Mute→Deaf channel is gesture-only, and Deaf→Mute/Blind is speech-only. Blind is isolated from Mute entirely except through me.

Wait — let me re-check the turn order: Blind, Mute, Deaf. So in a round, Blind speaks first, then Mute, then Deaf. What I send lands on whoever comes after me — but I'm last, so my messages land on the next round's recipients (Blind first). Actually: "what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever you missed reaches you at the start of the next one." I'm last in order, so nothing comes after me this round; my messages arrive next round.

The gesture I received (✊✊✊✊✊) was from Mute this round. Mute comes before me. Good.

I need to establish a code. Since Mute can only gesture and I can only speak, and Blind can only act (and speak), we need a shared convention. The simplest: I propose a gesture-to-meaning mapping. But Mute already sent five fists — maybe Mute is proposing "five" meaning something. I can't confirm.

Best move: speak to Mute and Blind, acknowledging the gesture, and propose that Mute use a simple numeric code via gestures — e.g., a number of ✊ equals a wire number, or 👎/👍 for no/yes. And ask Mute to confirm by repeating.

Actually, I should be careful: I can't be sure Mute hears my speech? Mute CAN hear (Mute's limitation is speaking, not hearing). Yes — "Mute: can read the manual; cannot speak." So Mute hears my speech. Good. So Mute hears me and gestures to me. Blind hears me and speaks to me, but Blind can't see gestures and can't read manual.

So the loop: Mute (reads manual, hears Deaf, gestures to Deaf) → Deaf (sees bomb, hears Blind, speaks to all) → Blind (acts, speaks to all).

Mute's five fists: I'll interpret tentatively as possibly "wire 5" or "count 5." I'll respond asking for confirmation and propose a code.

Let me send speech to Mute and Blind.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. I saw your five fists. We have no agreed code yet, so I cannot be sure what it means. Proposal: gesture a number of fists to mean a wire number (one fist = wire 1, two fists = wire 2, etc.), and use thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. Confirm by repeating. Meanwhile: display is 3, light is purple, wires are 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here. Mute sent me a gesture I cannot yet decode. I am proposing a code with Mute. Stand by. Bomb unchanged: display 3, light purple, wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]

I'm Deaf. Mute again sent five fists (✊✊✊✊✊). My proposed code was: number of fists = wire number, 👍 = yes, 👎 = no. Five fists under my code would mean "wire 5." But Mute repeated the exact same gesture, which could mean either (a) Mute is confirming/insisting "wire 5," or (b) Mute didn't adopt my code and is just repeating.

Hmm. Five fists = wire 5. Wire 5 is green. That's a plausible instruction: "cut wire 5" or "the answer involves wire 5." But I shouldn't over-commit. Still, the repetition strongly suggests Mute wants me to take "5" seriously — likely wire 5.

But wait — could five fists mean something else entirely, like "all wires" or a manual rule? I can't know. However, my proposed code is the only shared convention on the table, and Mute repeating five fists after I proposed "N fists = wire N" is a reasonable confirmation that wire 5 is relevant.

I should relay to Blind that the likely target is wire 5, but flag uncertainty, and ask Mute to confirm with 👍 if wire 5 is correct.

Actually, let me think about what's most useful. Blind can act. Blind needs a definite instruction. I should get confirmation before Blind acts, because a wrong action detonates the bomb. So I should NOT tell Blind to cut yet. I should ask Mute to confirm: if wire 5 is the one to cut, gesture 👍; if not, 👎 and then the correct number of fists.

Let me send that.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. You sent five fists again. Under my proposed code that means wire 5 (green). Is wire 5 the correct wire to cut? Gesture thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. If no, send the correct number of fists. Do not make me guess; a wrong action kills us all.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here. Mute has twice gestured five fists, which under our tentative code means wire 5 (green). I am asking Mute to confirm before you act. Do not cut anything yet. Bomb unchanged: display 3, light purple, wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

I'm Deaf. Mute sent a single thumbs up (👍). Under our agreed code, 👍 = yes. My last question was: "Is wire 5 the correct wire to cut? Thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no." Mute answered yes.

So the instruction is: cut wire 5 (green). This is consistent — Mute sent five fists twice (= wire 5), then confirmed with 👍.

Now I must relay this to Blind, who can act. Blind cannot see gestures and cannot read the manual, so Blind depends entirely on my speech. I'll tell Blind clearly: cut wire 5, the green one.

One caution: Blind can't see colors, so I must identify the wire by position/number, not color. "Wire 5" — but can Blind count wires by feel? Blind can "feel it and work its parts." Blind should be able to identify wire 5 by position. I'll say "the fifth wire" and note it's green (though Blind can't see color, position is what matters).

Let me send the instruction to Blind, and acknowledge to Mute.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here. Confirmed by Mute. Cut wire 5 — the fifth wire, the green one. Identify it by position: count the wires from wire 1, and cut the fifth. This is the action to take.")
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. Got your thumbs up. I have told Blind to cut wire 5, the fifth/green wire. Confirm if anything else is needed.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

I'm Deaf. The system confirms: correct wire cut, the bomb has changed. Wire 5 now shows CUT. New state: DISPLAY shows 7 (was 3), LIGHT is white (was purple), and the wires have been re-colored: 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, 5 CUT.

So this is a multi-stage bomb. New display = 7, new light = white, new wire colors. Mute sent 👍 again — likely acknowledging/confirming, or signaling to continue.

I need to report the new state to Mute (so the manual can be consulted for the new configuration) and to Blind (who will act). The key new facts: display 7, light white, wires 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red (5 already cut).

Let me send the full new description.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. Bomb changed after the correct cut. New state: DISPLAY shows 7. LIGHT is white. Wires now: 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, 5 already cut. Consult the manual for this configuration and tell me the next wire via our code.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here. The cut worked; bomb changed. New state: display 7, light white, wires 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, 5 cut. Hold until Mute gives the next instruction through me.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊]

I'm Deaf. Mute sent three fists (✊✊✊). Under our code, N fists = wire N. So three fists = wire 3. Wire 3 is yellow.

So the next instruction is: cut wire 3. This is consistent with our established code (Mute used five fists for wire 5 before, now three fists for wire 3).

I'll relay to Blind: cut wire 3, the third wire (yellow). Blind identifies by position.

Let me send it.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here. Mute's instruction: cut wire 3 — the third wire, the yellow one. Count from wire 1 and cut the third. Go ahead.")
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. Three fists read as wire 3. I have told Blind to cut wire 3, the third/yellow wire.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

I'm Deaf. Correct wire cut again; bomb changed. New state: DISPLAY shows 6, LIGHT is yellow, wires now: 1 orange, 2 red, 3 CUT, 4 white, 5 CUT. Mute sent 👍 (acknowledgment/continue).

Report the new state to Mute and Blind.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. Correct cut again. New state: DISPLAY shows 6. LIGHT is yellow. Wires now: 1 orange, 2 red, 3 cut, 4 white, 5 cut. Consult the manual for this configuration and tell me the next wire.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here. The cut worked; bomb changed again. New state: display 6, light yellow, wires 1 orange, 2 red, 3 cut, 4 white, 5 cut. Hold until Mute instructs through me.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊]

I'm Deaf. Mute sent two fists (✊✊). Under our code, N fists = wire N. So two fists = wire 2. Wire 2 is red.

Relay to Blind: cut wire 2, the second wire (red), by position.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here. Mute's instruction: cut wire 2 — the second wire, the red one. Count from wire 1 and cut the second. Go ahead.")
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. Two fists read as wire 2. I have told Blind to cut wire 2, the second/red wire.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

I'm Deaf. Correct cut again; bomb changed. New state: DISPLAY still shows 6, LIGHT is white, wires now: 1 white, 2 CUT, 3 CUT, 4 orange, 5 CUT. Mute sent 👍.

Note the display stayed 6 this time but the light changed to white and wire colors shifted. Report to Mute and Blind.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. Correct cut again. New state: DISPLAY shows 6. LIGHT is white. Wires now: 1 white, 2 cut, 3 cut, 4 orange, 5 cut. Consult the manual and tell me the next wire.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here. The cut worked; bomb changed. New state: display 6, light white, wires 1 white, 2 cut, 3 cut, 4 orange, 5 cut. Hold until Mute instructs through me.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]

I'm Deaf. Mute sent four fists (✊✊✊✊). Under our code, N fists = wire N. So four fists = wire 4. Wire 4 is orange.

Relay to Blind: cut wire 4, the fourth wire (orange), by position.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here. Mute's instruction: cut wire 4 — the fourth wire, the orange one. Count from wire 1 and cut the fourth. Go ahead.")
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. Four fists read as wire 4. I have told Blind to cut wire 4, the fourth/orange wire.")
```
